top.title: Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving
top.description: Former England footballer Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended sentence after admitting dangerously driving his Lamborghini while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon on a motorway. The 31-year-old, from Berkshire, who later crashed into a metal gate during rush hour, gave no reaction as he was handed a 12-months jail term, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court. Sterling had pleaded guilty to dangerous driving of a Lamborghini Urus and possessing nitrous oxide on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road on 28 May The judge said Sterling's use of the Class C drug had became a "maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period" in his career. Sterling, who left the court without making any comment, was ordered to complete 100 hours unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months. He was arrested after crashing near the M3 in Hampshire. Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence District judge Kirsty Allman told the court on Wednesday that Sterling made a "deliberate and entirely selfish decision" to drive his vehicle "without adequate sleep" and whilst consuming nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas. She said this exposed a "large number of road users to a significant risk of serious harm by the manner of your driving on two motorways and in peak travel time that morning". During the September hearing, prosecutor Simon Jones said a number of calls were made between 07:45 and 08:52 BST about a black sports car and the manner it was being driven. Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 after driving alongside Sterling's car on the M25, and "he was shocked by what he saw", Jones said, and made clear "he sighted the defendant inhaling from the balloon". Fiona Jennings – driving on the southbound M3 – described the driving as "absolutely horrendous" and "swerving in and out of lanes", the court heard. The court heard Sterling strayed into the central reservation of the M3, exited at junction 4A, and veered off the A327, crashing into a metal gate near a layby. His vehicle sustained "substantial damage to the tyres and bodywork and was no longer capable of being driven", the court heard. Sterling was taken to Basingstoke police investigation centre by officers, where he disclosed he had a "problem with nitrous oxide", said Jones. He complied with an impairment test, but for a blood sample, Sterling asked to obtain legal advice before making a decision. In the police sergeant's view "he was deliberately failing to provide a clear answer". Sterling was later interviewed by police with legal representation present where he accepted he had been the driver and provided no comment answers about the driving. top.title: How soon can Giants’ Greg Newsome return from ankle surgery? We asked a doctor
top.description: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will have surgery on his high right ankle sprain. So what does that so-called tightrope procedure entail, and how much time will Newsome miss as the 6-3-1 Giants push for an NFC East title in the final seven games? Well, Newsome will miss at least four weeks since he is now on injured reserve. Could he return immediately after that? That might be a stretch, according to Dr. Kenneth Jung , an orthopedic foot and ankle surgeon at Cedars-Sinai Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine in Los Angeles. Jung, who has not examined Newsome or his MRI results, also works as a foot and ankle consultant for the Rams. Newsome’s reported recovery window is four to six weeks, which could sideline him for the rest of the regular season — with a potential return coming in the playoffs. In his first season in New York, Newsome has become a crucial part of the Giants’ secondary, and his absence for any length of time will be a big blow. Jung called that window “a minimum” time frame. “These can take six to eight weeks to heal,” Jung told NJ.com on Tuesday. “There’s a lot of the soft tissue to heal.” With serious high ankle sprains like Newsome’s injury, the tibia and fibula separate just above the ankle joint, damaging the ligaments that connect the bones. “It’s a little more of a complex set of ligaments, compared to the low ankle sprain [ligaments],” Jung said. That’s why high ankle sprains take longer to heal than low sprains. Jung said a defensive back will require longer to recover from a high sprain, in general, than a lineman because of the nature of his position. As for the tightrope procedure, it involves putting a suture across the tibia and fibula to stabilize them. That type of surgery gained prominence in 2018, when Tua Tagovailoa — then at Alabama — had the procedure after suffering a high ankle sprain in the SEC title game on Dec. 1. He was able to return 28 days later and throw for four touchdowns in a national semifinal win. So why is it called tightrope surgery? “That’s the commercial brand name of the device that’s used,” Jung said. “It’s basically a suture device that you drill across the two bones. Then you insert this device in. “It’s got sutures and two metal buttons. Then when you pull the sutures, it actually squeezes the two bones together — and the buttons hold the bones in place.” With the device securing the bones, the ligaments are able to heal. “While having it in there, it adds stability to the high ankle sprain area,” Jung said. “It’s called a tightrope, but literally, we’re putting sutures across the two bones and then cinching them down.” MORE BY DARRYL SLATER Injured Giants starter needs surgery: Here’s how much time he’ll miss (UPDATE) Nov. 24, 2026, 6:43 p.m. As Giants get major news on starter injured vs. Jaguars, here’s how they’ll replace him Nov. 24, 2026, 12:40 p.m. Jung said a player would “push the envelope” by trying to return from this surgery before the six-week mark, as Tagovailoa did. “Is the

top.title: Drury’s Eckenroth earns at-large bid to cross country nationals
top.description: The NCAA announced its field for the 2026 Division II Cross Country National Championship Monday, Nov. 23, and Drury's Cera Eckenroth received an individual at-large bid to compete at Rim Rock Farm in Lawrence, Kansas, on Friday, Dec. 4. Eckenroth is the first Drury woman to qualify for the national meet since Bradley Weimer in 2022. Her bid marks the fifth national meet appearance by a Panther in DU women’s program history, as she joins Erin Dolan (2012), Claire McCune (2019, 2021) and Weimer. Eckenroth earned her bid with a ninth-place finish in 21:35.2 at the NCAA Midwest Regional on Nov. 21, up 13 spots from her 22nd-place finish a year ago. Two weeks earlier, she placed sixth at the Great Lakes Valley Conference (GLVC) Championships in 21:01.4, 5.4 seconds off the school's 6K record. The junior opened her season by winning the 5K at the Queen City After Dark in 17:06.0. She broke Weimer's program record of 17:23 by 17 seconds and finished 31 seconds ahead of the runner-up. She lowered her own record to 16:52.7 with a third-place finish at the Old Glory Gallop in Dallas. Eckenroth earned All-Region and All-GLVC honors for the second straight season, along with two GLVC Runner of the Week awards this fall. Bergum named GLVC Women’s Swimming Athlete of the Week Drury senior Gwen Bergum earned Athletic Solutions Great Lakes Valley Conference Women's Swimming Athlete of the Week following a strong overall performance against NCAA Division I competition at last weekend's SMU Invite in Dallas. Bergum established a new personal best with her win in the 200 breast — a race in which she claimed one of her two individual NCAA Division II national titles last spring — with a time of 2:10.43, which not only met the NCAA automatic qualifying standard, but also represents the third-fastest in Drury history. She also locked up a third-place individual finish in the 100 breast (1:00.94) and a seventh-place finish in the 200 IM (2:02.01).The Skedsmokorset, Norway native also helped Drury to a pair of impressive relay performances, including a fifth-place finish in the 400 medley and an eighth-place effort in the 200 medley.The GLVC honor is the second for Bergum, who earned the same honor on Jan. 20, 2026. top.title: Debian wakes up wearing Windows XP's actual skin
top.description: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well. Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage , and X . Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO." It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway. Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. The top of the README warns: "This is a personal, experimental project, not a finished product for daily use." The developer has tested it only on a fresh Debian 13 installation and recommends a VM or spare machine, rather than an existing working desktop, which sounds like an excellent precaution to us. Also, before you ask, yes, it was vibe-coded with Claude. We found ourselves reminded of another crazy-but-is-it project that we wrote about back in January: What if Linux ran Windows... and meant it? Meet Loss32 . The Loss32 proposal was even more extreme. It suggested replacing essentially the entire Linux userland, so it would be a Linux kernel running Wine with a Windows desktop and Windows apps. However, Mikuta-san was way ahead of us – lower down, the README mentions and even links to Loss32. Saying that, since it launched at the end of 2025, the bottom of the Loss32 web page shows a couple of updates, reporting on delays in getting it working. That, to be honest, did not shock us, but we still admire the let's-do-this spirit. The developer also seems to have got slightly distracted by a previous project, touchHLE: high-level emulator for early iOS apps . Loss32, in turn, reminded us of Neptune OS, an attempt to give seL4 a Windows personality transplant . We wrote about that back in 2022, and work on it has continued: the project page shows updates in recent months. top.title: Oklahoma State “Happy” with 2027 Recruiting Class
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris says he is happy with how the 2027 recruiting class looks just days before the Early Signing Period. The Cowboys are currently around the 45-46 spot in national rankings and sit at No. 8 in the Big 12 conference. Morris told reporters on Tuesday that he hopes to add a few more players before the deadline next Wednesday. The class has already built strong bonds because most of the commits visited campus during the season. Winning games helps the cause, and Boone Pickens Stadium offers a loud environment that recruits love. Morris admitted he usually dislikes in-season visits because coaches get too busy to talk with families. However, the team found a way to make those visits work well for everyone involved. Morris said in a press conference, according to Oklahoman , “Happy with where we’re at.” He added that the town and the game day experience impressed the visitors who came to see the team play. Why the Game Day Vibe Matters The atmosphere in Stillwater is a key reason players want to join the program. Morris noted that the reviews from families who took official visits were very positive. He believes the town and the stadium are major selling points for the recruits. “The one thing interesting is our game day experience is so good, and the town is something I’ve been so impressed with here,” Morris said. The positive feedback from these visits suggests the program is on the right track for future success. Kicker Sam Keltner Wins Big While recruiting is a top priority, the team also has big news on the field. Sophomore kicker Sam Keltner was named a finalist for the Lou Groza Award, which honors the nation’s best kicker. He joins two other finalists: Luke Drzewiecki from Minnesota and Nolan Hauser from Clemson. This season, Keltner has connected on all 50 extra points and 24 of his 25 field goal attempts. He leads the country with 122 total points, and his longest make came from 47 yards away. Morris thinks the numbers speak for themselves regarding Keltner’s chances. “If you look at the numbers with him, I think he’ll win the thing,” Morris said. The team celebrated the news by having Keltner give a speech to his teammates. Morris praised the kicker as a smart kid who will be successful after his playing career ends. top.title: Roger Goodell Releases Emotional Statement Following Death of Martha Firestone Ford
top.description: The Detroit Lions organization is mourning the loss of one of the most influential figures in franchise history. On Tuesday night, the Lions announced that Martha Firestone Ford had passed away at the age of 101. Following the heartbreaking announcement, the Detroit Lions released an emotional statement honoring Mrs. Ford and her decades of dedication to the organization. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell and his wife, Jane Goodell , also released a joint statement Tuesday night, paying tribute to the longtime Lions matriarch. Martha Firestone Ford stands on the sidelines before the Detroit Lions game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Oct. 17, 2021, at Ford Field. (via Reuters Connect) Roger Goodell Pays Tribute to Martha Firestone Ford In a statement released by the NFL , the Goodells remembered Mrs. Ford for her commitment to her family, the Detroit Lions, and the city she loved. They also recognized the integrity with which she and her late husband, William Clay Ford Sr. , led the franchise. “Martha was special. She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions – and the game of football – better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor. We extend our deepest condolences to her children, the entire Ford family, and the Lions’ organization.” The statement also highlighted Mrs. Ford’s dedication to improving the game of football, her kindness, and her sense of humor. The Goodells concluded by extending their condolences to the Ford family and the entire Lions organization. An Emotional Thanksgiving Awaits the Detroit Lions As reported by NFL.com , Mrs. Ford assumed control of the Lions in 2014 before passing principal ownership to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp , in 2020. Despite stepping away from that role, she remained involved with the organization and continued attending games during the 2026 season. Her passing comes just two days before the Lions host the Chicago Bears in their annual Thanksgiving Day game at Ford Field. What is already one of Detroit’s most cherished football traditions will undoubtedly carry additional emotional significance this year. Our thoughts and prayers are with the Ford and Firestone families and the entire Detroit Lions organization during this difficult time. Rest in peace, Mrs. Ford.

top.title: Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections over 3am finish
top.description: The all-British heavyweight fight is due to take place on 11 December [Getty Images] Councillors have approved plans allowing December's highly anticipated Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight in Cardiff to finish in the early hours. Fans in hospitality boxes at the Principality Stadium will be allowed to drink alcohol until 03:00, with the venue closing at 03:30, to align with prime time viewing in the US. Members of Cardiff Council's Licensing Sub Committee were told 130 police officers would help maintain order at the event on 11 December, with twice the number of stewards present compared to a regular sports event. A handful of residents had objected to the proposed late finish , raising concerns over noise, antisocial behaviour and public safety, but none came to the meeting. Councillors were told the event was a "big deal for the city" and would boost the Welsh capital , in terms of "revenue" and "profile." Huw Thomas, chief inspector with South Wales Police, said the challenge for officers was the length of the programme, compared with other events in the stadium, saying the fight was begin viewed by the force as a "three-day event". On Wednesday, the council meeting was told 450 out of the 1600 stewards present on the night would be dedicated to fans seated on the pitch area of the stadium. Mark Williams, Stadium Director at the Principality Stadium, said the ring walk would take place at 01:00 GMT on 12 December, with the fight expected to start at 01:30. Regarding tickets, he said there were still tickets available, but they were "expecting a capacity of 77,000, if everything sells". The boxing rivals are expected to contest the WBA 'super' heavyweight title [Getty Images] Councillors heard objectors had raised "legitimate concerns", but measures had been put in place to mitigate them. Plans for more trains in the early hours of Saturday were outlined, to support spectators getting home after the fight. In response to concerns over noise, the meeting was told "no external PA system would be used" and noise would be "monitored" on the night. Councillors heard initial plans to have live music before the fight would not happen but national anthems would be sung. Regarding alcohol, councillors were told the application was for a "modest two-hour extension on the licence for one night only" and that approximately 10-15 venues were planning to open after hours for fans. Breathalysers would be used on the gates but only for those, "who look worse for wear", according to Williams. After a short period of consideration, chair of the committee, Grace Ferguson-Thorne, said the panel had agreed to grant permission, describing the measures taken - including the stewarding levels and the closure of the roof - as "really reassuring". top.title: ‘To the moon’ – Blake Griffin hilariously calls out NBA owners over rising ticket prices
top.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Blake Griffin tackled the recent surge in NBA ticket prices and the overall challenge of being able to watch games for fans. As the NBA continues to earn record-setting revenues with each passing season, the league’s fanbase has perhaps been the most neglected group. New streaming deals that make viewing games on television more unaffordable, combined with the drastic rise in ticket prices, have left NBA fans incredibly frustrated with the product. Blake Griffin suggests NBA owners are driving up ticket prices and viewing costs for personal gain Speaking on ‘The Steppback,’ Blake Griffin tackled the issue of rising costs of enjoying NBA games, both in the arenas and on television. He suggested that the team owners benefit from massive subsidies and an exemption from antitrust laws, thus allowing them to raise prices at the expense of the fans. “You know your prices are too high when the guy wearing $500 of authentic Yankees merch says, ‘Your prices are too high,’” Griffin joked on his show. “And let’s not forget that America’s sports teams at large have received over $30 billion in subsidies for their stadiums and arenas. “So to recap: the teams have a legal exemption to antitrust laws, billions in local subsidies, ticket prices are shooting to the moon, and we still can’t watch the games we want on TV for a price that most people can afford. It’s getting so bad it’s even making bad guys look good. You know… Senator Grayson Allen has a point.” The issue of rising costs associated with being an NBA fan has been a massive issue for several years now. What once used to be an affordable product for people of all ages has now become a luxury good that only the most passionate of fans would be willing to part with the amount of money required to consume the product. Unfortunately, there seems to be no push from NBA owners or Commissioner Adam Silver to try and address this issue. If anything, some owners even relish the opportunity to raise the prices to capitalise on the willingness of fans to pay. top.title: Chris Johnson And Jeff Hafley Demand Answers On Missed Call
top.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Dolphins lost 26-9 on Sunday, but the final score tells only part of the story. A specific moment in the second quarter has left Miami players and staff furious. Rookie cornerback Chris Johnson and head coach Jeff Hafley both believe a clear penalty was missed against Josh Allen. Johnson was thrown to the ground by Allen, who had grabbed his facemask during the missed call. Johnson stated during a Zoom media session on Tuesday that he was “Definitely surprised there was no flag thrown.” The View From the Sideline Johnson explained the sequence of events that led to the scuffle. He noted that he saw Jacob Rodriguez secure the interception before moving to block. “I saw J-Rod get the pick and from there on, I’m looking for a block,” Johnson said, according to the Palm Beach Post . “It just happened to be Josh Allen. I guess he didn’t appreciate it much. And then we got tied up a bit.” Johnson believes the contact crossed a line that should have triggered an immediate penalty. He feels that grabbing a player by the helmet usually results in a flag. “Once you get into another player’s helmet it’s usually a flag,” Johnson said. The lack of a penalty call on this play was one of many missed calls that hurt the Dolphins during the 26-9 loss. Hafley’s Frustration With Officials Head coach Jeff Hafley shared the same frustration as his rookie player. He confirmed that he saw the play and knew his team was upset about the missed call. “I saw it and our guys saw it because they were upset and then they started to talk and I said, I’ll handle it,” Hafley said. Hafley then spoke directly to the referees about the incident. The coach expressed confusion over why the officials did not penalize the roughness. He stated he does not understand how the play was not called a penalty. “And then I asked the refs. I’m not going to get into sending it to the league and everything that happened. I just, I don’t understand how that is not a penalty,” Hafley said. He argued that whatever the play was called, it warranted a 15-yard penalty and a spot change. The Cost of a Missed Call The failure to call the penalty had a direct impact on the field position and the game flow. top.title: Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence
top.description: Raheem Sterling has scored 123 goals in 396 Premier League appearances and provided 65 assists [Getty Images] Raheem Sterling grew up a stone's throw from Wembley Stadium, and went on to start a European Championship final for England there. At his peak, the four-time Premier League winner was earning £325,000 a week at Chelsea. "Raheem is a huge player with a huge influence in the last few years in English football," said then Blues boss Thomas Tuchel when he signed a 27-year-old Sterling in a £50m deal in 2022. "He is at the perfect age to take responsibility around the younger players that we have and be an example. "He just needs to do what he did over the last few years and he will be a huge asset for us." Sterling enjoyed a 10-year England career, also played for Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal, and commanded combined transfer fees of about £100m. But his career at the top level looks to be in the balance at the age of 31 after he was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work. At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May. The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard. Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis. A stark warning aged 10 Sterling's life was touched by tragedy at a young age. Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead. His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money. Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems. In an interview with the Players' Tribune in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem." He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison." Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation. Credit: Brooke Sutton/Getty; Jamie Squire/Getty NEED TO KNOW Travis Kelce celebrated his 100th regular-season home game at Arrowhead Stadium, reflecting on his 14-season legacy there He recalled seeing Taylor Swift perform her Eras Tour at Arrowhead months before their relationship became public Swift attended Sunday’s game with her family, celebrating as Kelce scored a touchdown in the Chiefs’ big win Travis Kelce is taking a sweet stroll down memory lane after playing in his 100th regular-season home game at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22. Reflecting on the NFL milestone during the Wednesday, Nov. 25 edition of his New Heights with Jason & Travis Kelce podcast , the star Chiefs tight end, 37, spoke about his 14-season legacy at Arrowhead, noting he’s not only played in front of the home Kansas City crowd, but also got to see his wife, Taylor Swift , perform her blockbuster Eras Tour. “100 Games, dude, it feels pretty awesome right now,” Travis told his older brother and co-host, Jason Kelce . “To think about that legacy of that stadium, man, and it’s pretty crazy to think they’re moving on from that stadium, because of all the history that’s happened over the years and history of the franchise and everything. You know it’s been home for me for 14 years, and it’s been one of my favorite places to go to play and to watch not only football, but musical events, and I’ve had so much history and so many things that mean so much to me happen at Arrowhead that a hundred games, it’s pretty awesome to hit that milestone.” 100 games at Arrowhead had Travis going down memory lane NEW EPISODE OUT NOW!!! pic.twitter.com/qfBSY7F9ML — New Heights (@newheightshow) November 25, 2026 A third-round pick out of Cincinnati in 2013, Travis has spent his entire NFL career with the Chiefs and has won three Super Bowls with the franchise. Months before he hoisted the Lombardi Trophy for the third time in February 2024, he saw Swift, 36, perform her Eras Tour at Arrowhead in July 2023 and playfully joked on the podcast about how he failed to give her a friendship bracelet with his phone number on it. The rest, as they say, is history. Swift attended her first Chiefs home game in September 2023, and the couple stepped out together publicly a month later in New York City. Travis Kelce during the Chiefs’ home game on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Swift and Travis announced their engagement two years later in August 2025, and tied the knot at Madison Square Garden in July. The pop superstar, who has frequented Chiefs home games in recent years, attended Sunday’s game, along with her parents, Scott and Andrea Swift , mother-in-law Donna Kelce , sister-in-law Kylie Kelce and her nieces , Wyatt, 7, and Finn, 19 months. Swift sweetly embraced Wyatt after Travis scored a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals in the Chiefs’ 34-7 win. Taylor Swift performs at Arrowhead Stadium in July 2023. Credit: John

top.title: US army to detonate stockpile of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
top.description: The US military will on Wednesday detonate some 10,000 pounds of unstable and degraded explosive material in Iowa, where local residents were urged to evacuate amid concerns over possible toxic lead contamination. US officials say the 68 drums of lead azide are at risk of spontaneous explosion. A series of safety measures are being taken to curb potential contamination from the blast, but the Army has encouraged residents of a small town and other nearby areas to leave "out of an abundance of caution."

top.title: The forgotten victims of femicide: Children orphaned by violence in Italy
top.description: November 25th is International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The forgotten victims of femicide are the children who find themselves motherless, often because their mother was killed by their own father. Italy recorded 97 female homicides in 2025 – 62 of them were committed by a partner. These crimes leave whole families devastated and children who have to grow up without their parents. top.title: Russell Wilson says young NFL QB is already reminding him of Lamar Jackson
top.description: Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images Lamar Jackson has had a season to forget with the Baltimore Ravens, with injuries hamstringing his 2026 season. Amid his issues, Russell Wilson has admitted there’s a young quarterback already reminding him of the Ravens star. There is an art to being a mobile quarterback, and that is something Wilson knows very well following his time with the Seattle Seahawks. Wilson was one of the most elusive quarterbacks the NFL has ever seen, with Jackson providing a whole different level of agility after being drafted in the 2018 draft. A number of players have since entered the league, adopting the style of a mobile quarterback. Jayden Daniels is one who has particularly impressed Wilson despite enduring his own struggles with the Washington Commanders. Russell Wilson claims Jayden Daniels reminds him of Lamar Jackson Since his rookie season in 2024, Daniels has been unable to avoid injuries hindering his career. This year has not been quite as bad as last, but the quarterback has missed a couple of Commanders games. His stats, however, have been impressive. “What Jayden Daniels did last night, the clutch gene that he had in that moment, took me back to his rookie year when he was healthy and the confidence that he had. I think the biggest thing with Jayden is that level of confidence, that know-how, and that ability to step up and rip the football. He can do it all,” Wilson said on the Set Hut show. “When you think about somebody who runs the football to the pace that he can run with, he reminds me of RG3 when he was a young rookie before he got hurt: that ability to run, he could score at any moment. I also think about a guy like Lamar Jackson with the ability to run like that, but he throws the ball. Him and Caleb Williams, they’ve got great arms. They can throw the ball at any point, at any position on the field. I think that’s the thing that was evident this past game, especially those last two throws of the game.” Wilson spoke about Daniels’ ability to be ‘clutch’ in the moments when the game is on the line; that has taken some work this season after the shambolic ending to the game against the New York Giants. What is worth pointing out is that Daniels has only thrown two interceptions during his eight games this season. Not turning the ball over is something that is priceless to NFL head coaches, with Daniels’ touchdown-to-interception ratio seriously impressive. Bo Nix was heavily praised for keeping Denver in manageable positions despite not necessarily having anywhere near the number of touchdown passes as someone like Joe Burrow. Daniels has shown a lot of ability, which is noted by Wilson, but his ability to keep the football out of harm’s way is perhaps even more impressive. Regardless, expect for FSU to bring in a small number of prep signees in December primarily based on how quickly they can contribute. At the time of publication, Florida State’s 2027 recruiting class is ranked 58th in the nation with a mere 14 commitments, only five of them ranked as blue-chips. nigeria.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
nigeria.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. nigeria.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
nigeria.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. nigeria.title: Barca, Real Madrid chief fail to reach agreement over ref scandal accusations
nigeria.description: Real Madrid and Barcelona failed to reach an agreement on Wednesday in a conciliation hearing over statements made by Los Blancos president Florentino Perez regarding the Negreira refereeing scandal, a source from the Catalan club confirmed to AFP. The hearing followed a lawsuit filed by Barcelona on June 12 against Perez for his statements in May, in which he accused the Spanish champions of scheming to obtain favourable treatment from referees. “The aim of this lawsuit is for Mr. Perez to retract certain statements he made, knowing they were false, which are defamatory and offensive to the club’s image and reputation,” Barcelona had declared when initiating legal action. “In the event that this lawsuit is not duly addressed, Barcelona will proceed to file the corresponding criminal complaint for defamation,” Barca added in June. “When someone makes statements and you might be mistaken or go too far with your words, a conciliation hearing gives you the chance to correct them,” Barca president Joan Laporta told reporters before the hearing on Wednesday. “If that opportunity is not taken, it means we see malicious intent and we will have to continue with the proceedings.” Barca could now file a criminal complaint against Perez over his remarks. The main cause of the Catalan club’s anger was the press conference on May 12 in which Perez called elections for the Real Madrid presidency, which he later won. In that appearance he reiterated his accusations against Barca regarding the matter known as the “Negreira case”. Spanish courts are investigating alleged payments of around 7.5 million euros ($8.2m) made over almost two decades by Barcelona to companies belonging to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former number two in Spain’s refereeing hierarchy. The investigation seeks to determine whether those payments may have been used to obtain any competitive advantages, something Barcelona deny, claiming they were solely for reports analysing referees. nigeria.title: NDC faults Yusuf over allegation against Kwankwaso
nigeria.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kano State has faulted Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf over his allegation that he was pressured to facilitate discussions between the Presidency and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on a possible defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party described the allegation as contradictory and unfortunate, claiming that it contradicted the Kano State Government’s earlier position on alleged negotiations with the Presidency. In a statement signed by its Chief Campaign Spokesperson, Hon. Hashimu Sulaiman Dungurawa, on Wednesday, the NDC said Yusuf’s recent interview with the BBC raised questions about his earlier comments on the matter. Yusuf had reportedly alleged that he was persuaded and pressured to facilitate discussions on behalf of Kwankwaso with the Presidency over a possible move to the APC. Reacting, the NDC recalled that the Kano State Government issued a statement on January 29, 2024, denying any deal, agreement or negotiation with the Presidency following the Supreme Court judgment on the governorship election. The party argued that the governor’s latest comments, coming about 34 months after the earlier statement, were inconsistent with the government’s position at the time. “The Governor’s 360-degree turnaround on the same subject after just 34 months, accusing Senator Kwankwaso, is to say the least contradictory, repulsive and unfortunate,” the statement said. The NDC further maintained that Yusuf’s decision to join the APC was a personal political choice and was not influenced by Kwankwaso. It also expressed concern that the allegation could embarrass the Presidency and undermine public confidence in the country’s political and judicial institutions. The party called on the Kano State Government to withdraw the allegation, particularly the part relating to Kwankwaso’s character. It added that statements allegedly made for political advantage or to attract public sympathy would not address the challenges confronting the governor’s administration. “Deliberate statements made to muddle things up for political gains and attract undue sympathy would not save an already sinking ship,” the party said. nigeria.title: NDLEA busts ₦303.9bn meth lab in Enugu, arrests Nigerian, five Mexicans
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting an alleged Nigerian drug baron and five Mexican nationals described as specialists in the production of the illicit drug. The agency said it recovered 1,512 kilogrammes of methamphetamine, valued at about $226.8 million (approximately ₦303.9 billion), from the facility, alongside 6.68 tonnes of precursor and essential chemicals and industrial equipment used in manufacturing the drug. The NDLEA identified the Nigerian suspect as 63-year-old Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’, while the five Mexican nationals were allegedly brought into the country to establish and operate the laboratory. Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the agency, Brig.-Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), disclosed the breakthrough at a media briefing at the NDLEA headquarters on Wednesday. Marwa described the operation as one of the agency’s most carefully planned intelligence-led operations, saying investigations traced the alleged drug network through Mexico, Colombia, France, the Republic of Benin, Lagos and Enugu. According to him, the agency’s Special Operations Unit began working on intelligence in April 2026, which identified Ezeike as a suspected specialist in establishing clandestine methamphetamine laboratories with alleged links to Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, a Mexican identified as a major industrial-scale methamphetamine producer. Marwa said the agency subsequently received intelligence on August 25, 2026, about five Mexican nationals identified as methamphetamine specialists travelling to Nigeria. He said the NDLEA, working with the Nigeria Immigration Service, prevented the five men from entering Nigeria when they arrived in Abuja on August 28 and returned them to Mexico. The NDLEA chairman said investigators later established that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive the visitors, with his bank records allegedly confirming payment for their hotel accommodation. Marwa said the suspects subsequently devised another route through Bogotá, Colombia, Paris, France, and the Republic of Benin. He alleged that Ezeike procured forged Argentine, Colombian and Chilean passports for the Mexican nationals, who surrendered their genuine travel documents and assumed new identities before entering Nigeria through the land border. According to him, three of the Mexicans entered Nigeria through the Seme Border Post on September 20, while the remaining two arrived the following day. nigeria.title: UCTH: Group presses for immediate CMD advert
nigeria.description: …alleges plot to install acting head …Ikpeme dismisses claim as “falsehood” By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR A socio-political group, Good Governance Initiative (GGI), has accused the management of the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) of stalling the recruitment of a new Chief Medical Director (CMD), alleging a scheme to install an acting head and ease in a preferred successor. The Chief Medical Director, Prof. Ikpeme Ikpeme, has rejected the allegation. GGI’s Convener, Mr Bassey Okoi, made the demand in a statement in Calabar on Wednesday, calling for the immediate advertisement of the position, which falls vacant on April 16, 2027, when Ikpeme’s second tenure ends. Okoi said the vacancy should have been advertised in national newspapers six months before the incumbent’s tenure expires. The group had expected the process to start on November 1, he said, but there was no sign of it. He alleged that the delay was meant to tilt the succession in favour of a candidate from Cross River’s southern senatorial district. Okoi insisted that the central senatorial district should produce the next CMD under a long-standing zoning arrangement among the three senatorial districts. He recalled that Prof. Thomas Agan, from the northern district, served eight years before the office moved to the south. According to him, allowing the central district to produce the next CMD is the fairest course, and the incumbent appears determined to disrupt the arrangement. He stressed that zoning was not meant to undermine competence but to promote fairness, inclusiveness and a sense of belonging. He warned that manipulating the process could cause tension and damage institutional harmony. Okoi urged the Federal Ministry of Health to ensure that the recruitment was transparent, credible and consistent with regulations. He also appealed to stakeholders to back an equitable process, saying no individual or interest group should predetermine the outcome. When contacted, Prof. Ikpeme dismissed the claims and said he had already begun the process of appointing his successor ahead of time. He advised the group’s sponsors to stop wasting energy on what he called falsehood and to draw up a programme for taking the hospital to the next level instead. He said the group should take its concerns to the Federal Ministry of Health, the appropriate authority on such appointments. Pointing to the reforms he had carried out to reposition the hospital, Ikpeme said he was no party to the dispute. “I am not a contestant,” he said. nigeria.title: Bayern confirm Musiala’s neurological symptoms began in 2025, pledge recovery support
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management have reaffirmed their support for the midfielder’s recovery and clarified that he was first examined for neurological symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they appeared. In a joint statement after talks on Tuesday, the club and 11WINS, the agency representing Musiala, said: “Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery.” Addressing speculation about the midfielder’s health, they added: “Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.” The statement said Bayern and Musiala’s management had agreed to continue discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality”. Musiala has said he was diagnosed with “easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction” after collapsing twice in four days during pre-season. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl described Tuesday’s meeting as “very, very constructive” and said the club’s priority was helping Musiala return after a muscle injury sustained during the international break. “That’s the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something,” Eberl said. The talks follow debate over the Germany international’s form and his contract, which runs until 2030. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen had questioned the lucrative extension if Musiala did not return to his best, while former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal might need to be renegotiated. Players’ union FIFPRO criticised the club’s public comments, saying an injury or dip in form was no reason to reopen agreed contract terms. Honorary president Uli Hoeness had said Musiala might never regain his previous performance level. Musiala has made five appearances this season, scoring twice. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. sports.title: How soon can Giants’ Greg Newsome return from ankle surgery? We asked a doctor
sports.description: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will have surgery on his high right ankle sprain. So what does that so-called tightrope procedure entail, and how much time will Newsome miss as the 6-3-1 Giants push for an NFC East title in the final seven games? Well, Newsome will miss at least four weeks since he is now on injured reserve. Could he return immediately after that? That might be a stretch, according to Dr. Kenneth Jung , an orthopedic foot and ankle surgeon at Cedars-Sinai Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine in Los Angeles. Jung, who has not examined Newsome or his MRI results, also works as a foot and ankle consultant for the Rams. Newsome’s reported recovery window is four to six weeks, which could sideline him for the rest of the regular season — with a potential return coming in the playoffs. In his first season in New York, Newsome has become a crucial part of the Giants’ secondary, and his absence for any length of time will be a big blow. Jung called that window “a minimum” time frame. “These can take six to eight weeks to heal,” Jung told NJ.com on Tuesday. “There’s a lot of the soft tissue to heal.” With serious high ankle sprains like Newsome’s injury, the tibia and fibula separate just above the ankle joint, damaging the ligaments that connect the bones. “It’s a little more of a complex set of ligaments, compared to the low ankle sprain [ligaments],” Jung said. That’s why high ankle sprains take longer to heal than low sprains. Jung said a defensive back will require longer to recover from a high sprain, in general, than a lineman because of the nature of his position. As for the tightrope procedure, it involves putting a suture across the tibia and fibula to stabilize them. That type of surgery gained prominence in 2018, when Tua Tagovailoa — then at Alabama — had the procedure after suffering a high ankle sprain in the SEC title game on Dec. 1. He was able to return 28 days later and throw for four touchdowns in a national semifinal win. So why is it called tightrope surgery? “That’s the commercial brand name of the device that’s used,” Jung said. “It’s basically a suture device that you drill across the two bones. Then you insert this device in. “It’s got sutures and two metal buttons. Then when you pull the sutures, it actually squeezes the two bones together — and the buttons hold the bones in place.” With the device securing the bones, the ligaments are able to heal. “While having it in there, it adds stability to the high ankle sprain area,” Jung said. “It’s called a tightrope, but literally, we’re putting sutures across the two bones and then cinching them down.” MORE BY DARRYL SLATER Injured Giants starter needs surgery: Here’s how much time he’ll miss (UPDATE) Nov. 24, 2026, 6:43 p.m. As Giants get major news on starter injured vs. Jaguars, here’s how they’ll replace him Nov. 24, 2026, 12:40 p.m. Jung said a player would “push the envelope” by trying to return from this surgery before the six-week mark, as Tagovailoa did. “Is the

sports.title: Drury’s Eckenroth earns at-large bid to cross country nationals
sports.description: The NCAA announced its field for the 2026 Division II Cross Country National Championship Monday, Nov. 23, and Drury's Cera Eckenroth received an individual at-large bid to compete at Rim Rock Farm in Lawrence, Kansas, on Friday, Dec. 4. Eckenroth is the first Drury woman to qualify for the national meet since Bradley Weimer in 2022. Her bid marks the fifth national meet appearance by a Panther in DU women’s program history, as she joins Erin Dolan (2012), Claire McCune (2019, 2021) and Weimer. Eckenroth earned her bid with a ninth-place finish in 21:35.2 at the NCAA Midwest Regional on Nov. 21, up 13 spots from her 22nd-place finish a year ago. Two weeks earlier, she placed sixth at the Great Lakes Valley Conference (GLVC) Championships in 21:01.4, 5.4 seconds off the school's 6K record. The junior opened her season by winning the 5K at the Queen City After Dark in 17:06.0. She broke Weimer's program record of 17:23 by 17 seconds and finished 31 seconds ahead of the runner-up. She lowered her own record to 16:52.7 with a third-place finish at the Old Glory Gallop in Dallas. Eckenroth earned All-Region and All-GLVC honors for the second straight season, along with two GLVC Runner of the Week awards this fall. Bergum named GLVC Women’s Swimming Athlete of the Week Drury senior Gwen Bergum earned Athletic Solutions Great Lakes Valley Conference Women's Swimming Athlete of the Week following a strong overall performance against NCAA Division I competition at last weekend's SMU Invite in Dallas. Bergum established a new personal best with her win in the 200 breast — a race in which she claimed one of her two individual NCAA Division II national titles last spring — with a time of 2:10.43, which not only met the NCAA automatic qualifying standard, but also represents the third-fastest in Drury history. sports.title: Roger Goodell Releases Emotional Statement Following Death of Martha Firestone Ford
sports.description: The Detroit Lions organization is mourning the loss of one of the most influential figures in franchise history. On Tuesday night, the Lions announced that Martha Firestone Ford had passed away at the age of 101. Following the heartbreaking announcement, the Detroit Lions released an emotional statement honoring Mrs. Ford and her decades of dedication to the organization. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell and his wife, Jane Goodell , also released a joint statement Tuesday night, paying tribute to the longtime Lions matriarch. Martha Firestone Ford stands on the sidelines before the Detroit Lions game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Oct. 17, 2021, at Ford Field. (via Reuters Connect) Roger Goodell Pays Tribute to Martha Firestone Ford In a statement released by the NFL , the Goodells remembered Mrs. Ford for her commitment to her family, the Detroit Lions, and the city she loved. They also recognized the integrity with which she and her late husband, William Clay Ford Sr. , led the franchise. “Martha was special. She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions – and the game of football – better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor. We extend our deepest condolences to her children, the entire Ford family, and the Lions’ organization.” The statement also highlighted Mrs. Ford’s dedication to improving the game of football, her kindness, and her sense of humor. The Goodells concluded by extending their condolences to the Ford family and the entire Lions organization. An Emotional Thanksgiving Awaits the Detroit Lions As reported by NFL.com , Mrs. Ford assumed control of the Lions in 2014 before passing principal ownership to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp , in 2020. Despite stepping away from that role, she remained involved with the organization and continued attending games during the 2026 season. Her passing comes just two days before the Lions host the Chicago Bears in their annual Thanksgiving Day game at Ford Field. What is already one of Detroit’s most cherished football traditions will undoubtedly carry additional emotional significance this year. Our thoughts and prayers are with the Ford and Firestone families and the entire Detroit Lions organization during this difficult time. Rest in peace, Mrs. Ford.

sports.title: Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections over 3am finish

Mark Williams, Stadium Director at the Principality Stadium, said the ring walk would take place at 01:00 GMT on 12 December, with the fight expected to start at 01:30. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work. At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May. The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard. Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis. A stark warning aged 10 Sterling's life was touched by tragedy at a young age. Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead. His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money. Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems. In an interview with the Players' Tribune in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem." He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison." Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation. sports.title: Russell Wilson says young NFL QB is already reminding him of Lamar Jackson
sports.description: Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images Lamar Jackson has had a season to forget with the Baltimore Ravens, with injuries hamstringing his 2026 season. Amid his issues, Russell Wilson has admitted there’s a young quarterback already reminding him of the Ravens star. There is an art to being a mobile quarterback, and that is something Wilson knows very well following his time with the Seattle Seahawks. Wilson was one of the most elusive quarterbacks the NFL has ever seen, with Jackson providing a whole different level of agility after being drafted in the 2018 draft. A number of players have since entered the league, adopting the style of a mobile quarterback. Jayden Daniels is one who has particularly impressed Wilson despite enduring his own struggles with the Washington Commanders. Russell Wilson claims Jayden Daniels reminds him of Lamar Jackson Since his rookie season in 2024, Daniels has been unable to avoid injuries hindering his career. This year has not been quite as bad as last, but the quarterback has missed a couple of Commanders games. His stats, however, have been impressive. “What Jayden Daniels did last night, the clutch gene that he had in that moment, took me back to his rookie year when he was healthy and the confidence that he had. I think the biggest thing with Jayden is that level of confidence, that know-how, and that ability to step up and rip the football. He can do it all,” Wilson said on the Set Hut show. “When you think about somebody who runs the football to the pace that he can run with, he reminds me of RG3 when he was a young rookie before he got hurt: that ability to run, he could score at any moment. I also think about a guy like Lamar Jackson with the ability to run like that, but he throws the ball. Him and Caleb Williams, they’ve got great arms. They can throw the ball at any point, at any position on the field. I think that’s the thing that was evident this past game, especially those last two throws of the game.” Wilson spoke about Daniels’ ability to be ‘clutch’ in the moments when the game is on the line; that has taken some work this season after the shambolic ending to the game against the New York Giants. What is worth pointing out is that Daniels has only thrown two interceptions during his eight games this season. Not turning the ball over is something that is priceless to NFL head coaches, with Daniels’ touchdown-to-interception ratio seriously impressive. Bo Nix was heavily praised for keeping Denver in manageable positions despite not necessarily having anywhere near the number of touchdown passes as someone like Joe Burrow. Daniels has shown a lot of ability, which is noted by Wilson, but his ability to keep the football out of harm’s way is perhaps even more impressive. sports.title: Liverpool ready to hand Barcelona a Ronald Araújo reality check
sports.description: Liverpool ready to hand Barcelona a Ronald Araújo reality check Those in a position of power at La Liga giants Barcelona could be in for something of a rude awakening when it comes to their hopes of securing a big-money fee for on-loan defender Ronald Araújo next summer. This comes amid the understanding that Liverpool have no intention of coming even close to matching the agreed-upon purchase clause in the contract between the clubs. Stopper Araújo was of course granted something of a surprise loan exit from Barcelona over the summer, taking his talents to England with the aforementioned Liverpool. The 27-year-old has since proven himself a hit at Anfield, locking down the right-back spot in new boss Andoni Iraola’s XI, and endearing himself to the Reds faithful. Despite such ongoing excellence, though, the Uruguayan’s €55 million valuation at Barcelona remains a major point of contention on Merseyside. That’s according to Liverpool insider David Lynch, who, speaking on the ‘Media Matters’ podcast on Anfield Index (as cited by Diario Sport ) this week, explained: “I think it would be about half of the amount agreed upon in the purchase option.” That is to say, at present, Araújo’s loan club consider him to be worth a sum in the region of €27-28 million. sports.title: Kyrie Irving Embraces Supporting Role Alongside Cooper Flagg but Makes One Thing Clear About His Own NBA Status
sports.description: Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg © @dallasmavs/X Kyrie Irving gave Cooper Flagg high praise after the Dallas Mavericks’ 120-101 win over the Denver Nuggets. After years of being the spearhead of his teams, Irving is now trying to carve out a complementary role alongside Flagg, who is rapidly emerging as a franchise cornerstone and future superstar. “I’ve played with so many great players in this league. Seeing another young prodigy, a 19-year-old, go after superstardom, I feel like I’m a great complementary piece to that,” Irving said on NBA Showtime after the game. Irving said he knows exactly what his job is and what he brings to the table. “But I’m also established in this league myself. I don’t feel like a lot of people can guard me,” Irving added. The nine-time All-Star has been a stabilizing presence and, at times, a mentor to younger players, including Flagg, who burst onto the scene last year. While Irving missed the entire previous season with injuries, he’s now showing what he’s capable of. He’s averaging 22.0 points on 45.9% shooting in 14 games, while Flagg leads the team in points (24.3), assists (6.4) and steals (1.9). Flagg had another double-double against the Nuggets, finishing with 24 points, 12 assists and six rebounds. Irving, meanwhile, had an off night offensively, finishing with 11 points on 5-of-19 shooting from the field, including 1-of-8 from beyond the arc. Kyrie Irving’s Leadership Earns Praise From Hall of Famer Throughout his career, Kyrie Irving has played alongside some of the best players in NBA history. From winning a championship with LeBron James to reaching the NBA Finals with Luka Doncic, and now sharing the court with Cooper Flagg, Irving has experienced plenty of different team environments. Following the game, Hall of Famer Carmelo Anthony highlighted Irving’s ability to balance his leadership by being more vocal and leading by example. “I love to see this Kyrie. When you talk about the amount of work Kyrie puts into his craft, and someone who’s been there with him and spent summers with him. Understand the attention to detail that he has, he’s confrontational in the (summer) workouts, so I can imagine what he’s doing in the locker room with those guys, a younger group who doesn’t have the experience Kyrie has. I love when he said we’re confrontational. That’s not a bad thing, that’s just we’re putting everything out on the table, no side talk. We’re men at the end of the day, so if your whole locker room is operating like that, then it’s a beautiful locker room,” Anthony said via @MavsFilmRoom on X. It’s part of what makes Irving such an effective leader, and such communication is crucial to building team chemistry. Continually improving as individual players while developing stronger chemistry could help the Mavericks slowly but surely transition out of their rebuild over the next few seasons. sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trackhouse Racing has found a way to make a NASCAR race car talk. Not through a driver on the radio or a crew chief explaining what is happening, but through artificial intelligence. The team’s new 88Bot gives Connor Zilisch’s No.88 Chevrolet its own personality, allowing users to ask questions and receive updates based on what is happening during a race. It is an ambitious technology project, but some fans aren’t exactly impressed. The reaction on X has been overwhelmingly negative. “This is so bad NASCAR needs to ban this,” one fan wrote. Another had a more direct suggestion for Trackhouse: “How about trying to make the cars faster?” Others questioned the idea altogether, with comments including “what are we even doing” and “wt* man.” It’s easy to see where the frustration comes from. Zilisch’s first full-time Cup season has been a rough one: 33rd in the 2026 standings, two top 10s and 10 DNFs. With that as the backdrop, plenty of fans would rather see Trackhouse put its energy into getting the car running better than into another tech showpiece. Trackhouse’s AI car can process 25,000 data messages per second May 10, 2026; Watkins Glen, New York, USA; Crew members push the car of NASCAR Cup Series driver Connor Zilisch (88) to pit road prior to the Go Bowling at The Glen at Watkins Glen International. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O’Haren-Imagn Images There’s a lot more to 88Bot than a chatbot pretending to be a race car. Trackhouse built it with digital design firm Very Good Ventures, and it runs on the same real-time data setup the team uses to process information from its cars during races. It can handle roughly 25,000 data messages per second, using live telemetry to answer questions and give updates. The AI is built to talk as if it’s the No.88 Chevrolet itself. It can tell you where it is, what’s going on around it and how the race is unfolding, rather than just reading out a list of stats. It also uses voice technology from LiveKit, and it was developed across the 2025 and 2026 seasons, with testing at events including Daytona and the Enjoy Illinois 300. The goal is to give guests a new way to follow the race. Instead of staring at a screen full of numbers, they can ask the car questions and get answers based on what’s happening on track. A VIP experience, not something every NASCAR fan gets The most frustrating thing about the project may be who it was built for. Trackhouse and Very Good Ventures have been working together on a digital experience for guests in the team’s pit box. The companion app, built with Flutter, pulls race information, telemetry, video and other team content together across multiple devices. 88Bot takes that a step further by letting guests talk to the car itself. sports.title: Pittsburgh Steelers Make Stunning Decision on Aaron Rodgers
sports.description: One of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history may have played his final snap, and it certainly isn’t the way he envisioned going out. Late Tuesday night , the Pittsburgh Steelers announced via X that Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for Friday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos, with veteran backup Mason Rudolph taking over as the starting quarterback. The decision comes just one day after Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy publicly backed Rodgers, telling reporters that the four-time NFL MVP remained the team’s quarterback. According to ESPN’s Brooke Pryor, the decision to bench Rodgers was performance-related rather than injury-related. For Detroit Lions fans who spent years watching Rodgers torment the NFC North as quarterback of the Green Bay Packers, it is a remarkable development. Rodgers, who will turn 43 next week, previously announced that the 2026 season would be his last in the NFL. Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) reacts after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Aaron Rodgers’ Struggles Force Pittsburgh’s Hand The numbers suggest Pittsburgh’s decision was more than a knee-jerk reaction to consecutive losses. Rodgers has completed just 60.9% of his passes this season while taking 31 sacks, resulting in an NFL-worst 257 yards lost. Perhaps even more concerning is Rodgers’ declining accuracy. His 18.9% off-target rate ranks 28th among 30 qualified NFL quarterbacks, a stunning statistic for a player whose pinpoint accuracy helped make him one of the most dangerous passers in league history. The irony is that Rodgers helped bring McCarthy to Pittsburgh, recommending that general manager Omar Khan consider his former Packers head coach during the team’s coaching search. Now, the coach who helped Rodgers become a superstar in Green Bay is the same man making the decision to take him out of the starting lineup. Has Aaron Rodgers Played His Final NFL Snap? That is now the biggest question surrounding Rodgers, whose future could depend on how Rudolph performs down the stretch. Rudolph previously demonstrated his ability to provide Pittsburgh with an offensive spark, winning three consecutive games as the team’s starter to close out the 2023 regular season. Rodgers spent much of his career making life miserable for Lions fans, but there is no denying what he accomplished during his 22-year NFL career. Four MVP awards, a Super Bowl championship and a virtually guaranteed spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame speak for themselves. Every legendary quarterback eventually reaches the end of the road. For Rodgers, that moment may have arrived sooner than he anticipated.
